title: Nodal curves are etale local on the source
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{h_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family (every point of $X$ is the image of a point of some $U_i$) of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Call a morphism nodal of relative dimension one if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is purely one-dimensional [def-weil-pure-dimension], and every nonsmooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $f$ is nodal of relative dimension one if and only if every $f\circ h_i$ is nodal of relative dimension one. There are no quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian assumptions; the family may be empty when $X$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0C5D, lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source, and preceding Tag 0C5C; lines 4778--4847

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-source-fibre-preparation] to the given jointly surjective etale family. Its two equivalences give flatness and local finite presentation of $f$ exactly when all composites have them. In either implication, the assumed nodality supplies local finite presentation on the assumed side, hence on both sides. Fix any algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. Put $C=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $D_i=U_i\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The lemma identifies $D_i$ with $U_i\times_X C$ over $C$; the maps $e_i:D_i\to C$ form a jointly surjective etale family, and $C,D_i$ are locally finite type over $\Omega$ and locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0C5D, lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source, structural descent and geometric-fibre preparation (old steps 1--4); descent.tex Tags 036K lemma-flat-fpqc-local-source and 036N lemma-locally-finite-presentation-fppf-local-source; algebra.tex Tag 05G5 lemma-base-change-finiteness (4); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 lemma-finite-type-noetherian

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-cover-field-curve-nodality] to this cover with $k=\Omega$; step 1 supplies all its hypotheses. With $n=1$ its purity equivalence gives pure dimension one for $C$ exactly when all $D_i$ have it. Under this condition, if the nonsmooth nodal condition holds on $C$, every nonsmooth $y\in D_i$ maps to a nonsmooth $x\in C$ by the smoothness equivalence; the completion equivalence gives the condition at $y$. Conversely, lift each nonsmooth $x\in C$ to some $y\in D_i$ by joint surjectivity. The same two equivalences make $y$ nonsmooth and give the nodal completion at $x$ from that at $y$. Empty fibres have no irreducible components or points, so the fibre conditions there are vacuous. As $\Omega,g$ were arbitrary, both fibre clauses are equivalent for every geometric fibre. Together with step 1 this proves the stated iff.

source.place: Tag 0C5D, lemma-nodal-family-etale-local-source, dimension and singularity argument over a field (old steps 5--8); descent.tex Tag 04N4 lemma-dimension-at-point-local and Tag 04NL lemma-dimension-at-point; varieties.tex Tag 0A21 lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (3), (5); curves.tex Tag 0C57 lemma-node-etale-local; descent.tex Tag 036U lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, each map $U_i\to X$ forces $U_i$ to be empty. Flatness and local finite presentation are then vacuous pointwise conditions, and each geometric fibre has no points or irreducible components to test. Thus both sides hold. A jointly surjective empty family forces $X$ empty, covering the empty-family case.
